components.source_clause: For all real a,b, the genuine matrix quadratic at every vector and at (1,t); PSD iff a>=0 and b=0.
hypotheses: Arbitrary real a,b; no positivity or PSD conclusion assumed.
components.per_clause_reason: The literal symmetric 2x2 matrix is used. Its actual matrix-vector quadratic expands to a*x^2+2*b*x*y, so the hint gives precisely a+2bt. Both necessity and sufficiency for genuine all-vector PSD are proved; the converse uses the actual diagonal PSD criterion.

components.source_clause: If b is nonzero choose t of the opposite sign and sufficiently large magnitude to make the true quadratic negative.
hypotheses: Arbitrary real a and nonzero real b.
components.per_clause_reason: The actual t=-(|a|+1)/(2b) has b*t<0 and |t|>|a|/(2|b|) for every real a. Its true matrix quadratic is exactly a-|a|-1<0. This supplies the literal sign and magnitude proof route, including negative a; the previous -(a+1)/(2b) witness alone would not establish that route for every a.

components.source_clause: A singular-corner generalized Schur rule needs the genuine Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse and range condition as well as its PSD remainder.
hypotheses: Arbitrary finite real left/right vector spaces; actual symmetric D (mandatory for a symmetric PSD block). No invertibility or strict positivity of D.
components.per_clause_reason: Actual spectral decomposition constructs the true pseudoinverse, including zero eigenvalues, and proves all four Moore-Penrose equations. For arbitrary finite real block sizes the actual matrix is PSD iff D is PSD, range(B transpose) is included in range(D), and A-B Ddagger B transpose is PSD. The range condition is derived from kernel annihilation in necessity and supplies a genuinely invertible block square-completion in sufficiency. No Schur conclusion or range conclusion is supplied as a theorem premise.

components.source_clause: The zero corner has true pseudoinverse0, whose remainder-only test misses b=0.
hypotheses: Arbitrary finite real blocks for the zero-corner iff; exact Fin1/Fin2 a=b=1 for the explicit false positive.
components.per_clause_reason: The true zero-matrix pseudoinverse is0 and its actual range condition is exactly B=0. Thus the genuine block PSD test reduces to B=0 and A PSD. The literal a=b=1 example has positive remainder1 while its actual original 2x2 matrix is not PSD, proving the stated incomplete-test defect rather than only a numeric analogy.

components.source_clause: An invertible corner has full actual range and its true pseudoinverse is its inverse, so the definite version needs no extra range check.
hypotheses: Arbitrary finite real symmetric corner; IsUnit D or D positive definite for these conditional consequences.
components.per_clause_reason: Every target vector is explicitly attained by D inverse times that vector, proving actual range(D)=univ. Positive definiteness gives actual invertibility and therefore the range inclusion for every B. The Moore-Penrose identity and actual inverse derive Ddagger=D inverse, giving precisely the source definite-corner interpretation.

material_units.source_text: The quadratic form at $(1,t)^\top$ is $a+2bt$. If $b\ne0$, choosing $t$ with the opposite sign and sufficiently large magnitude makes it negative. Therefore PSD forces $b=0$. Once $b=0$, the matrix is PSD exactly when $a\ge0$.

material_units.source_text: Using a pseudoinverse of the zero corner gives only the condition $a\ge0$ and misses the necessary $b=0$. The general semidefinite Schur-complement rule needs a range condition in addition to the pseudoinverse. The definite-corner version avoids this issue because an invertible corner has the entire space as its range.
